raw_hypothesis.name: ADX_GATED_RSI_MEAN_REVERSION_WEEKLY_METALS
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: In low-trend regimes (ADX14 < 25), RSI14 extreme oversold readings on weekly gold/silver bars mark genuine overshoot points that revert toward the 20-period moving average, because a trend-strength gate removes the cases where an oscillator extreme reflects continuation rather than exhaustion. Weekly bars aggregate enough price information that noise-driven false extremes are rarer than on intraday timeframes.
raw_hypothesis.rationale_vs_graveyard: Distinct from the graveyard's MEAN_REVERSION variants (failure_pattern=grid-shift-artifact): those failed because entry signals were anchored to fixed candle-count lookbacks that don't survive wall-clock grid shifts. Weekly bars have only one plausible convention (calendar week close), which removes most of that grid-alignment ambiguity by construction rather than requiring a re-derivation. Distinct from the graveyard's RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION (failure_pattern=sample-too-thin): that project's own diagnosis found real, mechanistically-corroborated value in a confirmation-style filter but tested it on the thinnest config (BTC/1d, 7-19 trades) instead of its own best, least-thin results (GOLD/1week and SILVER/1week). This hypothesis targets exactly those already-flagged-as-less-thin weekly metals series directly, using a simple ADX-gate + RSI-extreme trigger (no range/support-resistance definition that would starve the sample further), and avoids adding any ranking/selection layer on top (the mistake diagnosed in CARRY_MOMENTUM).
raw_hypothesis.companion_variant_note: A symmetric short setup (adx14 lt 25 AND rsi14 gt 70, exit on close cross_below ma20) could be tested as a mirror case for completeness.
raw_hypothesis.evaluation_focus: Compare against random-entry baseline on the same ADX<25 filtered candle set to isolate whether the RSI extreme trigger itself adds timing value beyond just being in a low-trend regime.

raw_hypothesis.name: BB_SQUEEZE_ATR_EXPANSION_BREAKOUT
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: When ADX14 is low (non-trending / compressed market state) and price then crosses above the upper Bollinger Band, the breakout tends to continue for several bars because the preceding low-trend compression represents genuine accumulation rather than noise, and the ADX-low gate specifically targets the transition moment from compression to expansion rather than entries into an already-established trend.
raw_hypothesis.rationale_vs_graveyard: Distinct mechanism from the graveyard's BOS_CONTINUATION (failure_pattern=regime-filter-only): that mechanism used a swing-point structure-break trigger where the capped 3.0x ATR stop was diagnosed as dominating over the intended structural stop in 75-95% of trades, meaning it was really just generic trend-following with an ATR stop wearing a structural-break label. This hypothesis uses a volatility-band trigger (Bollinger upper band cross) with ATR sizing as the explicitly intended stop mechanism from the outset, not a fallback overriding a different intended stop, so it doesn't inherit that specific diagnosed dilution. Distinct from FVG_REVERSION (failure_pattern=edge-over-random-negative): this is a continuation/expansion play driven by volatility-compression state (ADX gate + band breakout), not a fair-value-gap reversion play, and uses a different information source entirely.
raw_hypothesis.companion_variant_note: A symmetric short variant (adx14 lt 20 AND close cross_below bb_lower, mirrored ATR stop/target) could be tested as a mirror case.
raw_hypothesis.evaluation_focus: Compare against a random-entry baseline restricted to the same ADX<20 compressed-regime candles, to isolate whether the band-breakout trigger itself adds timing value beyond simply being in a low-ADX regime (avoiding the 'regime-filter-only' failure pattern by testing the trigger's marginal contribution explicitly).

raw_hypothesis.name: MA200_TREND_FILTER_PULLBACK_LONG_EQUITIES
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: Among large-cap tech/growth stocks on daily bars, when price is in a confirmed long-term uptrend (close above ma200) and pulls back to touch or dip slightly below the 20-period moving average without RSI collapsing into deeply oversold territory, that pullback offers a higher-probability continuation entry than either chasing new highs or trading with no trend filter at all. This exploits the well-documented tendency of price above a 200-day moving average to be associated with continued positive drift, combined with a shorter-term pullback entry for improved risk/reward versus breakout entries.
raw_hypothesis.rationale_vs_graveyard: Distinct from the graveyard's TREND_PULLBACK filter variants (FVG-overlap, BOS-recency; failure_pattern=edge-over-random-negative): those added FVG-overlap or BOS-recency filters on top of a pullback entry, and the BOS-recency filter was diagnosed as a functional no-op because breaks of structure occur too frequently within a 20-candle window to be selective. This hypothesis uses a completely different, much coarser and far less frequently-flipping filter -- the 200-period moving average trend gate -- and applies the pullback-in-uptrend mechanism to single large-cap US equities on daily bars (a different asset class than the crypto/FX pairs previously tested for TREND_PULLBACK), testing whether the mechanism transfers to trend-persistent large-cap equities where 200-day MA regime filtering has substantial documented support in trading literature. It is also distinct from MACRO_RISK_ON (failure_pattern=mechanism-doesn't-transfer) by staying entirely price-technical and asset-specific rather than relying on a macro regime signal.
raw_hypothesis.notes: The rsi14>35 condition on entry is meant to distinguish a healthy pullback from the early stage of a trend-breaking decline, avoiding entries into deteriorating momentum even though close is still nominally above ma200.
raw_hypothesis.evaluation_focus: Compare against a random-entry baseline restricted to the same close>ma200 uptrend-regime candles, to isolate whether the ma20 pullback + RSI>35 trigger adds real timing value beyond simply being long in an uptrend (avoiding the regime-filter-only failure pattern by testing the trigger's marginal contribution explicitly).

raw_hypothesis.name: VOLUME_CONFIRMED_MA20_BREAKOUT
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: A breakout above the 20-period moving average accompanied by rising volume signals genuine participation behind the move rather than a low-conviction cross, and such volume-confirmed breakouts have higher continuation rates than breakouts on flat or declining volume. Applied to crypto (BTC, BNB) and liquid large-cap equities (AAPL, NVDA, TSLA) where traded volume is a meaningful signal, using a close cross_above ma20 trigger gated by volume exceeding the prior bar's volume as a simple rising-participation filter.
raw_hypothesis.rationale_vs_graveyard: This targets an information source -- traded volume -- that none of the listed graveyard mechanisms (FVG_REVERSION, BOS_CONTINUATION, FUNDING_EXTREME, EMA-trail exit, TREND_PULLBACK filter variants, LEADLAG_FOLLOW, MEAN_REVERSION variants, MACRO_RISK_ON, CARRY_MOMENTUM, RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION, Vol-Clustering position sizing, LIQUIDATION_PREDICTOR, REPAIR_BREAKOUT_QUALITY) used as a primary entry gate. It is mechanistically distinct from BOS_CONTINUATION (a price-structure break trigger) by using a simple moving-average cross gated on a liquidity/participation confirmation instead of a structural swing-point trigger, so it does not inherit the diagnosed capped-ATR-stop-dilution problem, since the ATR stop here is the explicitly intended risk control from the start.
raw_hypothesis.notes: The DSL's listed volume field appears to be a single current-bar value; a strict 'above N-period average volume' condition may not be directly expressible without a volume moving-average field. This proposal frames the filter as volume greater than the previous bar's volume as the simplest DSL-expressible proxy for rising participation; if only a raw volume-vs-fixed-threshold comparison is supported, per-asset threshold calibration would need to happen outside this proposal.
raw_hypothesis.evaluation_focus: Compare against an MA20-cross-only baseline without the volume filter, and against a random-entry baseline on the same candle set, to isolate whether the volume-confirmation step itself adds real timing value versus just being a generic MA breakout (directly testing for the edge-over-random-negative failure pattern seen repeatedly in the graveyard).

raw_hypothesis.hypothesis_name: ADX-Confirmed Volatility Breakout (BB Upper/Lower Break with Trend-Strength Filter)
raw_hypothesis.mechanism: Classic Bollinger Band breakouts (price closing outside the bands after a low-volatility contraction) are prone to false breakouts/whipsaws when the underlying market has no real directional conviction. Web research on this exact combination (BB breakout + ADX confirmation) reports that adding an ADX trend-strength filter to a raw squeeze-breakout meaningfully improves quality by rejecting breakouts that occur in choppy, low-ADX regimes. This differs from the graveyard's BOS_CONTINUATION (structural swing-point break, diluted by a capped ATR stop) and REPAIR_BREAKOUT_QUALITY (already failed) by using a volatility-band trigger rather than a structural swing-point trigger, and by requiring a currently-elevated ADX (adx14 > 25, a real trend already establishing) rather than any structure-break event, which the graveyard diagnosed as too frequent/non-selective. The RSI ceiling (rsi14 < 70 for longs) is added to avoid entering right at exhaustion/blow-off-top conditions where the breakout is already extended. This is a bidirectional hypothesis (long on upper-band breaks, short on lower-band breaks) tested on a liquid trending asset.
